long_biography.plain_text:
San José began as a Galician building and rehabilitation business before Jacinto Rey became its chief executive in 1987. Under his leadership, the company added civil works, entered Portugal and other overseas markets, and acquired businesses that broadened its reach. A merger with Parquesol provided a route to Spain's stock market in 2009 and created a listed platform for the next phase.

Rey now exercises 48.29 percent of the voting rights and continues as executive chairman, distinct from his son Jacinto Rey Laredo, the group's first vice-president and construction chairman. Building contracts still dominate the order book, covering hospitals, transport infrastructure and complex engineering works. Renewable-energy services, concessions and project management provide additional lines, making him an active controller rather than a passive family shareholder.

uncertainties.detail: Grupo SANJOSE's history dates the business to 1962, before Rey's documented executive appointment. Contemporary reporting identifies the Gándara family as founders and Rey as an early accountant who became chief executive and controlling owner. The dossier therefore does not call him the founder despite some later secondary articles using that shorthand.

The operating ascent and later controlling ownership support a self-made classification, and no Rey-family inheritance was found. Public sources do not explain the financing and timing of every share acquisition, so the dossier does not assign the more specific independent-start or advantaged-start subtype.

Jacinto Rey González is the executive chairman and principal shareholder. His son Jacinto Rey Laredo is first vice-president and chairman of SANJOSE Constructora; a second son, Javier Rey Laredo, is second vice-president. Records describing the vice-president or the construction-subsidiary chairman must not be attributed to the upstream owner.

The Spanish corporate-governance page labels Rey presidente y consejero delegado, while the English governing-body page separately names José Luis González Rodríguez as chief executive. The proposed known-for title uses Executive Chairman, the unambiguous current role, and does not imply that Rey is the only chief executive.

The group also operates in energy, environmental services, concessions and project management. Construction remains the primary classification because the company calls it the main activity and it accounted for most of the latest reported order book; the other sectors remain secondary context.

Pontevedra and 1951 are supported by Spanish business reporting and the Forbes identity context. The upstream month is January, but no strong public source reviewed supplied the exact day, so no birth-day proposal is made.

No exact personal LinkedIn, Instagram or personal website was verified. The official Grupo SANJOSE website is proposed as the company website; the Forbes España article is not proposed as a personal profile.

Vessel reporting is used solely to resolve the exact upstream identity. Political associations and photographs involving other people, volatile market values, current wealth estimates and individual contract awards are excluded from the biographies and classifications.

The exact full name, Pontevedra company chain and 43-metre vessel match resolve the identity conclusively. The conservative wealth account is a self-made operating ascent to control of a construction-led group, with secondary sectors kept separate. No compiled or live state was changed.
